verdictRule.perPose: over-budget = absent = checksum-mismatch = build-failure = 0, AND every V3T-eligible member is either drawn by the near or mid tier, suppressed under a drawn far-tier tile, or named in the committed exemption set.
verdictRule.readFrom: The eight data-far-tier-* per-state counts, plus data-far-tier-massing-suppressible / -covered / -uncovered for the member-level half.
verdictRule.stillsAre: CONTEXT, NOT EVIDENCE. A screenshot cannot show that a count is zero. The counts are the evidence and the stills are labelled non-evidentiary.

sweeps.registeredBefore: CORRECTED. An earlier revision of this section claimed it was 'written before any pose of sweep-2 was read'. THAT WAS FALSE and is withdrawn: this prose — the settle rule, the vehicle note and the discarded-capture disclosure — was authored AFTER the six captures were taken. PRE-REGISTERED IN COMMIT 3c5c64f, before any screen was looked at: the six poses, their URLs, the exemption set, the attempt policy and the verdict rule — everything that DECIDES a verdict. Those pose definitions were reused UNCHANGED for sweep-2 and were not re-chosen after sweep-1's failure, which is the property that matters and which a reader can verify against 3c5c64f.
sweeps.provenance: Run after the P2 coverage-race fix, commit 200446c10b199a542feed11f3f6f4ba6008aa194 ('The P2 "coverage race" was a stale publish, not a lost write'), on a production build (pnpm build + pnpm preview) of that commit plus the default flip.
sweeps.whySweep2Exists: Sweep-1 FAILED at P2. That FAIL is preserved in sweep-results.json unedited and is NOT superseded, withdrawn or re-scored. Sweep-2 is a second, separately registered measurement of the same poses against a changed build; both stand in the record.
sweeps.attemptPolicy: SINGLE accepted capture per pose. A capture is ACCEPTED only when the settle rule below is met; an unsettled capture is a failure to capture, not a verdict, and is disclosed rather than silently replaced.

settleRule.statement: BLIND TO THE VERDICT — it never inspects `uncovered` — and fixed before any ACCEPTED capture. Stated precisely because the adjacent `discardedCapture` disclosure would otherwise contradict it: the rule was WRITTEN AFTER the first capture pass was discarded for measuring an unloaded scene, not before the first pose was ever read. It was then applied uniformly to all six accepted captures. PRE-REGISTERED IN COMMIT 3c5c64f, before any screen was looked at: the six poses, their URLs, the exemption set, the attempt policy and the verdict rule — everything that DECIDES a verdict. A settle rule decides only WHEN a reading is taken; it cannot be tuned toward a number it is structurally unable to see.
conditions: data-far-tier-massing-active > 0 — the dense layer has committed, so there is a scene to measure at all.
The triple (active, suppressible, covered) is IDENTICAL across three consecutive reads 8 s apart.
settleRule.cap: 240 s. On expiry the capture is recorded as NOT SETTLED.
settleRule.offArmExemption: P6-OFF is exempt from the active>0 condition: with the tier off there is no far-tier status element and suppressible is 0 by construction, which is the arm's whole point.
settleRule.whyThisRuleAndNotADwell: Sweep-1 used a fixed 48 s dwell and one of its two disclosed instrument defects was a settle judgement that fired on a dense-rebuild plateau. A fixed dwell cannot tell 'finished' from 'paused'.

discardedCapture.statement: DISCLOSED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. A first capture pass on 2026-08-21 using a fixed 50 s dwell was discarded before any verdict was taken.
discardedCapture.reason: P1 produced no far-tier status element at all, and P2 read data-far-tier-massing-active = 0 with data-far-tier-applied-covered = 0 while desired-covered was 23,992 — the dense layer had not committed, so the reading measured an unloaded scene rather than the pose.
discardedCapture.whyThisIsNotARetry: `uncovered` was 0 in that P2 reading. Accepting it would have been a FALSE PASS in the direction of the outcome being sought; discarding it moved the reading AWAY from the desired answer, not toward it. The settle rule was then written to make the precondition explicit and applied uniformly to all six poses.
discardedCapture.whatWasNotDone: No pose was re-read after a verdict was seen. No pose was re-read to change a verdict.

vehicle.differenceFromSweep1: SWEEP-1 RAN ON `vite dev`; SWEEP-2 RAN ON A PRODUCTION BUILD. This is a real difference in vehicle and is stated rather than glossed: the production build is what a user would receive, and it is the stricter of the two for this measurement, but the two sweeps are therefore not byte-identical vehicles.
